checks.claim: A submarine dives by flooding its ballast tanks with seawater and surfaces by blowing them out with compressed air.
checks.why: HowStuffWorks: vents open and water floods the main ballast tanks to dive; compressed air from flasks blows the water out to surface.

sources.title: How does a submarine dive, resurface and navigate underwater - ScienceABC

checks.claim: A submarine's thick pressure hull keeps the deep water pressure from crushing it.
checks.why: Wikipedia: the pressure hull of thick high-strength steel with ring stiffeners withstands the outside pressure.

checks.claim: A propeller at the stern pushes a submarine through the water.
checks.why: Patent background: submarines are propelled by a propeller-based system at the stern.

sources.title: US patent 6427618: jet-propelling a submarine (background on stern propellers)
Why Navies Keep Submarine Propeller Designs So Secretive - SlashGear

checks.claim: A periscope lets a submarine crew see above the surface while the submarine stays under water.
checks.why: A periscope lets a submarine at shallow (periscope) depth search the surface and air while the hull stays submerged.
